ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against PBOC domestic PEP database, SAMR administrative penalty and blacklist records, NMPA regulatory debarment registers, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, UN Security Council consolidated asset freeze and travel ban lists, EU and UK consolidated sanctions, and Taiwan's restricted-party and export-control lists. The screening must cover the Taiwan corporate entity, its 25% and above UBOs, all directors, supervisors, senior managers, and major trading counterparties in the ophthalmic supply chain, using fuzzy 70% name-match algorithms plus human review. Cross-strait red flags such as close-kin PEP status or adverse media concerning medical device procurement shall trigger escalation to the AML compliance partner and, if unresolved, a Suspicious Activity Report to the China Financial Intelligence Monitoring Center.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) and the local Market Regulation Bureau's online enterprise name pre-registration platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Chinese legal name must adopt the four-tier format: administrative division + distinctive trade token + industry or operating characteristics + organizational form (Limited Liability Company). The English name is a non-registrable reference translation and must be a faithful transliteration or translation of the Chinese trade token; pinyin romanization is accepted but must not infringe third-party trademarks. All governmental records, tax invoices, customs declarations, and bank accounts must reference the approved Chinese name. Any proposed English name that transcribes a foreign trademark must be accompanied by a trademark use authorization.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: China/Chinese (as prefix without State Council approval)
Misleading clinical benefit claims (Restores Vision, Cure Guarantee)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant shall first obtain a written decision citing the exact similarity conflict and legal basis. An administrative reconsideration petition must be filed with the SAMR at the next higher level within 60 days of the refusal, or an administrative lawsuit filed with the competent People's Court within 6 months. The applicant may concurrently file a replacement name application with a new distinctive token, but cannot claim back the original name unless the conflicting registration is cancelled or amended. If the rejection was based on lack of distinctiveness, the appeal must be supported by a trademark search report and market recognition evidence. Formal written response to the appeal is due within 30 working days; no further extension is available except for extenuating circumstances.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding mailbox is categorically impermissible for a manufacturing WFOE of this industry. SAMR requires a physical registered address matching the production site; the State Taxation Administration rejects virtual addresses for VAT general taxpayer and invoice quota purposes; and the bank AML/KYC department will demand the original lease contract (minimum 12 months), site visitation, and production equipment photographs before making the UBO declaration. Because ISIC 3250 involves cleanroom manufacturing of Class III implantable medical devices, the registered office must coincide with the actual plant location and hold a current property use permit for industrial/medical production.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified likelihood: 85% within the first 12 months after registration. Checklist for unannounced on-site inspection: (1) production machinery (CNC lathe, polishing platform, hydrophobic coating unit) present and operable; (2) ISO 13485/GMP-compliant cleanroom and environmental monitoring log; (3) the company signboard bearing the approved Chinese legal name; (4) original lease, utility bills and payroll records; (5) on-site quality management personnel; (6) acceptance purchase orders for raw PMMA/collamer materials; (7) compliance with fire safety and medical-device traceability rules. Municipal tax, NMPA, and SAMR authorities coordinate random inspections under the double-random open-check system.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), Articles 23-25, 30, 41-48, 55-60; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 12-19; Regulations on the Protection and Encouragement of Investment by Taiwanese Compatriots; Regulations on the Administration of Market Registration (State Council Order No. 746); Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Medical Device Manufacturing Enterprises (State Administration for Market Regulation order implementing NMPA registration procedure).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation, Enterprise Registration Bureau, exercised through the local Administration for Market Regulation of the province or district where the wholly foreign-owned enterprise is established; filings are made at the government affairs enterprise registration one-window or the national unified enterprise registration online platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Enterprise (Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration and Business License Application Form).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a WFOE limited liability company under PRC law. The registered capital is set in the Articles of Association and the full subscribed amount must be contributed within five years from the date of establishment under Article 47 of the 2023 revised Companies Law. A blocked escrow account is not generally required, but contributed capital must be received into the company's basic bank account and the contribution must be reported under the foreign investment information system. Because the business scope covers Class III medical device manufacturing, the paid-in capital must be sufficient to equip and operate the intraocular acrylic lens production facility at the time the Medical Device Production License is audited.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: AT A DULY SUMMONED, QUORUM-CONSTITUTING, AND VALIDLY HELD FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (the Company), a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company organized under the laws of the People's Republic of China, held on [DATE] at [VENUE], the directors present in person or by proxy constituted a quorum as required by the Articles of Association. The Chairman declared that notice of the meeting had been duly given to every director, that the agenda had been circulated with the notice, and that the board was competent to transact the business before it. RESOLVED, that the authorized registered capital of the Company be fixed at [AMOUNT] in [CURRENCY], divided into [NUMBER] shares of registered capital of [PAR VALUE], and that the initial shareholder subscribe for the full amount at par in accordance with the capital contribution schedule stated in the Articles, with full payment to be completed no later than five years from registration under the Companies Law of the People's Republic of China. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Company adopt and maintain its registered office at [FULL ADDRESS], within the jurisdiction of the [LOCAL ADMINISTRATION FOR MARKET REGULATION], and that the General Manager be authorized to execute all documents and to file all registrations connected with such office. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Company's books and accounts be kept in Renminbi, and that [BANK NAME] be appointed as the principal bank of the Company. The legal representative, the General Manager, and the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly or severally, are authorized to open, maintain, operate, and close the Company's basic deposit account, capital account, foreign currency accounts, and any other accounts; to execute account opening applications, remittance mandates, letters of credit applications, loan documents, and related banking agreements; and to give binding payment instructions on behalf of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons are hereby appointed as statutory officers for the terms and with the responsibilities provided in the Articles of Association: [LEGAL REPRESENTATIVE], [CHAIRMAN], [GENERAL MANAGER], [SUPERVISOR], and [COMPANY SECRETARY IF APPOINTED]. Each officer shall hold the office until removal by written resolution of the shareholder or a subsequent valid meeting of the board of directors. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the legal representative, the General Manager, and the Chairman be and they hereby are jointly and severally authorized to sign all contracts, leases, licenses, permits, government filings, tax returns, environmental impact assessment applications, medical device registration submissions, and any instruments necessary to effect the incorporation and licensing of the Company, and to perform all acts that may be necessary, proper, or convenient to implement the resolutions herein adopted. RESOLVED FURTHER, that these resolutions be retained as a record and certified by the Secretary, and remain in full force and effect until revoked or amended by a later valid resolution of the board of directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Verification and Cross-Strait Investment Eligibility Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation, Enterprise Registration Bureau, through the national unified enterprise registration online platform or the district government affairs center enterprise registration counter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed corporate names in the registration system for automatic duplicate check and legal compliance screening. The reviewing officer verifies that the business scope described as ISIC 3250, manufacture of foldable hydrophobic intraocular acrylic lenses, does not appear in the Foreign Investment Negative List or the special restrictions applicable to Taiwanese investors. If the proposed name is acceptable and the scope is unrestricted, the name is preliminarily reserved for a finite statutory window. The investor must provide notarized identity documents, a Taiwanese investor certificate where the ultimate investor is domiciled in Taiwan, and a power of attorney appointing the local incorporator. Any query must be answered through the online filing system within the prescribed correction period.
required_dossiers: Completed enterprise name pre-registration application
Proposed corporate name list (up to three names)
Notarized investor identification certificate or certificate of incorporation
Taiwanese enterprise registration or company profile certificate, if ultimate investor is Taiwan-based
Power of attorney appointing the local formation agent
Written consent for use of the proposed name and business scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application is queried or suspended, submit a curing amendment through the same online portal within five working days, such as revising the name to avoid confusion or narrowing the business scope wording. If the authority issues a formal refusal, file an administrative reconsideration application with the same-level people's government or the next higher market regulation authority within sixty days, or bring an administrative lawsuit within six months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution, and Notarization of Formation Documents and Registered Office Proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary office in the intended registered-office jurisdiction and retained corporate legal counsel; no government filing is made during this preparation phase.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association, shareholder subscription agreement, first board resolution, and supporting corporate governance documents. The Articles must specify the corporate name, domicile, business scope, capital contribution schedule, governance organs, legal representative, supervisor, transfer restrictions, procedures for annual reports, and liquidation arrangements. Secure a lease or certificate of ownership for the physical registered office, with a lease term of at least one year, and obtain the building owner's written consent if required by local regulations. Notarize the investor's execution of the subscription agreement and the board authorization, and complete cross-strait notarization and authentication of the Taiwanese investor's corporate records where applicable.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Shareholders' subscription agreement and capital contribution schedule
Pro-forma first board resolution
Certified copy of the registered-office lease or property ownership certificate
Building owner's written consent for business use
Investor board or shareholders resolution authorizing establishment of the WFOE
Notarized power of attorney for the local agent
Legalized or authenticated Taiwanese investor documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the lease or ownership proof is defective, replace it with a valid property certificate and lodge the corrected document in the subsequent registration filing. If the notary refuses authentication because of incomplete capacity evidence, cure the defect by supplying updated investor resolutions or certified translation within ten working days and then re-notarize before proceeding to the AMR application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Incorporation Filing with the Administration for Market Regulation and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation, Enterprise Registration Bureau, via the government affairs center one-window service or the national enterprise registration online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Enterprise together with the adopted Articles, subscribed capital schedule, first board resolution, notarized investor documents, registered-office lease, legal representative identity documents, and appointment forms for officers. The AMR will verify the name reservation, screen the business scope against negative-list restrictions, examine the legality of the Articles, and register the company in the national enterprise credit information system. Upon approval, the AMR issues the business license, which is the founding deed, and the uniform social credit code is generated simultaneously. The company is deemed legally established on the date of issuance, after which it may apply for the subsequent tax, bank, and industry-specific operating licenses.
required_dossiers: Name reservation approval notice
Application for Establishment Registration of Foreign-Invested Enterprise
Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
First board of directors resolution
Legal representative identification and appointment certificate
Supervisor appointment and identity document
Investor qualification certificate and power of attorney
Certificate of use of registered premises, including lease and property title
List of statutory officers and basic contact information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMR returns the application for correction, cure the specific deficiencies stated in the issuance error list within five to fifteen working days by resubmitting the corrected electronic dossier through the same portal. If the authority suspends or refuses registration, request written reasons, apply for administrative reconsideration within sixty days under the Administrative Reconsideration Law, or file an administrative lawsuit within six months at the competent people's court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Seals, Tax Registration, Bank Account Opening, and Foreign Exchange Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-approved seal engraving enterprise; local branch of the State Taxation Administration; qualified bank authorized to open basic deposit and foreign exchange accounts; social insurance, housing fund, statistics, and foreign exchange administration departments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the business license, carve the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, contract seal, and legal representative seal at an engraving company designated by the local Public Security Bureau, and record the seal impressions with the AMR. Complete tax registration with the local taxation authority, including information collection of taxpayer status, invoicing types, and tax-filing methods. Open the company's basic deposit account in Renminbi and, where necessary for cross-strait invested capital, a foreign currency capital account with an approved bank; file the bank account number with the taxation authority. For Taiwanese investment, perform the foreign exchange or cross-strait investment reporting through the receiving bank under the State Administration of Foreign Exchange regime. Finally register with the social insurance agency, housing-fund agency, statistics department, and the annual reporting system that consolidates information for the AMR and tax authorities.
required_dossiers: Business license and uniform social credit code certificate
Public Security Bureau seal engraving application and approval notice
Legal representative identity certificate
Articles of Association and certificate of incorporation
Tax registration information sheet and bank account application forms
Board authorization for signatories to banking agreements
Foreign exchange registration questionnaire or cross-strait investment reporting form
Lease and site-usage proof required by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration or bank account opening is delayed because of an on-site inspection requirement, provide the lease agreement, floor plan, and photographs of the registered office and request an expedited inspection appointment. If the bank queries the source of funds or governing authorization, cure by supplying the notarized investor resolution, board resolution, and updated Articles and reissue the account-opening request within the bank's hold period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Medical Device Production Licensing and Pre-Production Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Medical Products Administration and its delegated provincial Medical Products Administration; local Administration for Market Regulation for industrial enforcement; municipal ecology and environment bureau and fire and rescue authority for environmental and civil-defense approvals.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commercial production of foldable hydrophobic acrylic intraocular lenses, the company must obtain a Class III Medical Device Registration Certificate for the product and a Medical Device Production License for the manufacturing site. Prepare the complete product technical file, biological safety and biocompatibility data, sterilization validation protocol, cleanroom qualification records, ISO 13485 quality management system documentation, and clinical evaluation or exemption basis. Submit the application through the NMPA online portal, pay the statutory review fee, and undergo a quality-system audit by NMPA inspectors, who will verify manufacturing equipment, cleanroom environmental controls, raw material traceability, and batch production records. The production license will issue only after the facility passes the GMP inspection, and concurrent environmental acceptance and fire-safety completion records must be available for verification.
required_dossiers: Class III medical device registration application
Product technical requirements and draft labeling
Test reports from NMPA-recognized testing laboratory
Biocompatibility and sterilization validation reports
ISO 13485 quality manual and GMP compliance records
Cleanroom layout and ISO 14644 validation certificate
Manufacturing process flow, equipment list, and validation protocols
Environmental impact assessment approval and self-acceptance report
Fire safety acceptance certificate and civil defense completion record
Occupational hazard pre-evaluation and control-effect evaluation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NMPA issues a deficiency letter, submit supplementary technical, clinical, or cleanroom validation data within the specified remedy deadline, normally fifteen to thirty working days. If the factory inspection fails, implement a corrective action plan covering equipment, records, contamination control, or personnel training, then request a reinspection at the next available regulatory slot. If the license is refused, pursue administrative reconsideration before the NMPA or the State Administration for Market Regulation within sixty days, or judicial review before the competent people's court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) and provincial Medical Products Administration for medical device manufacturing; local Administration for Market Regulation for production supervision; municipal ecology and environment bureau for environmental permits; local fire and rescue authority for civil defense clearance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Production License (Medical Device Manufacturing License) and Class III Medical Device Registration Certificate for foldable hydrophobic intraocular acrylic lenses, together with Municipal Environmental Permit and Fire Safety Acceptance Certificate before production start.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China and provincial/municipal Bureau of Ecology and Environment exercising delegated approval.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Report (Class I, Report of Environmental Impact Statement) under the Graded Management List of Environmental Impact Assessment for Construction Projects, because the acrylic lens production involves organic-solvent extraction, monomer feedstock handling, and volatile organic compound emissions below the applicable sulfur dioxide threshold but still within the reporting category for medical device manufacturing with chemical solvent use.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater pH 6-9, COD no higher than 100 mg/L, BOD5 no higher than 30 mg/L, SS no higher than 70 mg/L under the Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard unless a stricter local discharge agreement applies; stack exhaust non-methane total hydrocarbons (NMHC) no higher than 30 mg/m3 and treatment efficiency no lower than 90% under GB 37822-2019, with factory-boundary NMHC not exceeding 2 mg/m3; hazardous waste including acrylic resin waste and solvent residues must be classified, stored in an approved separate containment area, manifested, and transported only to a licensed hazardous waste disposal facility with a maximum storage period of one year.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire protection design review, fire acceptance filing, and fire safety certification from the local fire and rescue authority; civil defense approval and structural load inspection where the production area is below grade; occupational hazard pre-assessment and control-effect evaluation under the Law on the Prevention of Occupational Diseases covering noise, volatile organic compounds, and micromachining dust; work-safety facility three-simultaneous approval under the Work Safety Law; cleanroom environmental conformity inspection for controlled manufacturing areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online portal: Electronic Tax Service Platform (E-Tax) operated by STA and provincial tax service bureaus, accessible through www.chinatax.gov.cn.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Taiwan-resident investor forms the Chinese WFOE through the Administration for Market Regulation. The issued business license contains the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which functions as the WFOE statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration identifier under the multi-license integration system. Within 30 days of license issuance, the legal representative and finance officer must complete supplementary tax registration through the Electronic Tax Service Platform by confirming the competent tax authority, industry classification (medical device and intraocular lens manufacturing), accounting standards, fiscal period, bank deposit accounts, and controller details. The platform issues an electronic filing password, CA certificate and tax-control U-Key for e-filing and invoice issuance. The WFOE must then apply for general VAT taxpayer status if estimated annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000 or on a voluntary basis, apply for invoice quota and electronic invoice issuance rights, and complete export tax rebate registration in the E-Tax platform. For the Taiwan shareholder as a non-resident enterprise without a Chinese establishment, the WFOE as withholding agent must complete non-resident enterprise registration with the STA to obtain a non-resident TIN for dividend, interest and royalty withholding; the Taiwan shareholder may also be required to provide a Taiwan tax residency certificate when invoking cross-strait tax arrangement relief.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the Chinese WFOE is a resident enterprise for Corporate Income Tax purposes, taxed at entity level on worldwide income at the statutory 25% CIT rate, and is not eligible for pass-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists under PRC CIT. Under VAT, a small-scale taxpayer may elect to register as a general VAT taxpayer if accounting and compliance conditions are met, and a general VAT taxpayer may elect simplified VAT calculation only for enumerated categories at 3% or 5% as statutorily specified; no pass-through election is available for the WFOE.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC VAT legal framework; no separate GST or sales and use tax applies on the WFOE manufacturing and export activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales in any continuous 12-month period triggers mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration; there is no separate VAT registration turnover threshold for the WFOE because the USCC automatic tax registration applies from incorporation, and the threshold determines small-scale versus general taxpayer classification.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the Golden Tax Project Phase IV, requiring all VAT invoices to be issued through the tax-authority-controlled e-invoice system using the taxpayer U-Key or CA certificate. Fully digitalised electronic invoices are generated in the STA electronic invoice service platform and carry a real-time digital anti-counterfeit signature before transmission to the buyer; invoice data, VAT returns, customs export declarations, and SAFE foreign-exchange collection records are automatically cross-matched. A VAT special invoice for input credit is valid only if it has cleared through the national invoice system and is included in the taxpayer invoice verification records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A general VAT taxpayer exporting intraocular acrylic lenses from mainland China, including sales to Taiwan, is eligible for the 0% VAT export rate, with input VAT refundable, provided the goods are physically exported from mainland Chinese customs territory; the export is made by the WFOE with a valid customs export declaration; the export sale is supported by an export invoice, sales contract, transport document, and input VAT special invoices; and the export proceeds are received from the Taiwan or other overseas buyer in foreign exchange, repatriated to China through a designated foreign exchange bank, and recorded in the SAFE trade-in-goods system. The Taiwan buyer is generally liable for Taiwan import business tax at importation, and the WFOE does not acquire a Taiwan indirect-tax registration solely by exporting goods to Taiwan unless it creates a fixed place of business in Taiwan.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: China Customs Export Goods Declaration form (exit declaration) with electronic release record
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing physical departure from mainland China
Export commercial invoice and packing list
Export sales contract or purchase order identifying the Taiwan or overseas buyer, Incoterms and payment terms
Export invoice (ordinary VAT invoice/zero-rated export invoice) issued by the WFOE
Bank foreign exchange receipt and export proceeds collection record in the SAFE trade-in-goods monitoring system (functional FIRC-equivalent in China)
Input VAT special invoices for raw materials, components and production overheads used in the exported lens production
Export tax rebate declaration and export-to-invoice matching list as filed through the Electronic Tax Service Platform
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and China Customs use Golden Tax data analytics to cross-check export invoices, customs declarations, and SAFE foreign-exchange collection data. If export zero-rating or refund substantiation fails, the STA disallows the refund, claws back the refunded VAT, and charges late-payment surcharge at 0.05% per day. Under the Tax Collection Administration Law, fraudulent export tax refund imposes an administrative penalty of one to five times the amount fraudulently refunded; false customs declarations may also trigger Customs penalties. Where the fraudulent amount reaches RMB 50,000, the case is referred for criminal prosecution for fraudulent export tax refund, carrying imprisonment and heavy fines, with life imprisonment for especially large amounts. The recovery period for fraudulent refund claims is unlimited, while non-fraud errors are generally subject to the statutory three-year assessment limitation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a dual-tier foreign exchange convertibility regime. The RMB is fully convertible for current account transactions, including cross-border trade in goods, services, trade-related insurance, and profit remittances for this CN_WFOE_LTD, subject to genuine transaction background and SAFE-verified documentation. Capital account items remain tightly controlled. The Taiwan parent's registered capital contribution is classified as foreign direct investment and must be registered with SAFE, released through the FDI capital foreign-exchange account, and settled into RMB only against real operating expenses under the real-transaction settlement principle. Profit remittances are permissible after the annual audit is completed, corporate income tax is paid, and SAFE declaration formalities are fulfilled; the WFOE must demonstrate actual business substance, submit audited Chinese GAAP financial statements, and obtain a tax clearance certificate from the PRC tax authority. Export proceeds from the sale of intraocular acrylic lenses are current account items and may be settled voluntarily, but the foreign-exchange income must be repatriated to China and reported in the Trade in Goods Foreign Exchange Monitoring System. Major hurdles arise where capital injections exceed the registered FDI amount, where shareholder loans are used to circumvent capital controls, or where cross-border guarantees create outbound contingent liabilities requiring prior SAFE filing or registration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's Trade in Goods Foreign Exchange Administration Rules, export proceeds arising from customs-cleared exports must be repatriated to China and credited to the exporter's domestic foreign-exchange settlement account or foreign-exchange account within 180 days from the date of export customs declaration, unless SAFE grants an extension for documented force majeure, payment dispute, or abnormal trade-cycle reasons. The mandatory conversion ratio is 0% for Class A exporters, who may retain the foreign currency or voluntarily sell it to a domestic bank at market rates. For Class B or C exporters, SAFE may impose enhanced verification, require full supporting documentation for every collection, and in practice require 100% purchase-and-surrender or a verifiable settlement justification for each export receipt until the enterprise's compliance status is upgraded.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally barred as primary banking rails. Offshore digital EMIs cannot open a domestic RMB current account, cannot hold a SAFE-registered FDI capital account, cannot perform foreign exchange settlement under China's Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations, and cannot issue or confirm commercial letters of credit under PRC banking law. Such platforms may be used only for ancillary cross-border receivables collection through a licensed PRC third-party payment institution, subject to settlement limits and full sweeping to the onshore Tier-1 bank account. Any attempt to operate the WFOE's corporate treasury, capital injection, or trade settlement exclusively through an offshore EMI would create an unlawful unlicensed payment structure and cause SAFE and PBOC to reject the account relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical appearance is required for the WFOE's legal representative at the PRC bank branch. PBOC's administrative measures on bank settlement accounts require original corporate chops, original business license, passport or identity card, articles of association, board resolutions, and a face-to-face interview with the branch compliance officer. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted by Tier-1 Chinese banks for a newly formed, high-risk medical-device WFOE. If the legal representative is outside mainland China, the bank may accept a notarized power of attorney, but the authorized officer must still appear in person with original identification and the bank may require a video interview for additional verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial owner across the Taiwan-China cross-strait ownership layers, especially if the Taiwan investor holds shares through nominee entities, family trusts, or an offshore SPV.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Taiwan corporate registry of the direct shareholder, audited share register or ledger, certified passports of all natural-person UBOs, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations, formal beneficial ownership declaration identifying each UBO and percentage, and notarized board resolutions approving the formation of the Chinese WFOE.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk medical-device industry classification triggering enhanced scrutiny because intraocular acrylic lens manufacturing involves special licences, hospital counterparties, and complex reimbursement flows susceptible to trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: NMPA medical device registration certificate, medical device production license, ISO 13485 quality certificate, CFDA-validated product technical file, full projected customer and distributor list, sample purchase and distribution contracts, commercial invoice templates, customs clearance samples, and an internal AML counterparty risk-rating policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital remittance from Taiwan cannot be directly traced to the Taiwanese investor's own bank account, or the capital injection arrives very soon after incorporation with no economic explanation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements of the remitting Taiwan shareholder, audited financial statements of the Taiwan parent, notarized shareholder resolution approving the FDI injection, SAFE or bank-issued FDI registration certificate, SWIFT MT103 remittance instruction clearly naming the WFOE as beneficiary and referencing the FDI equity-injection purpose code, and a Chinese CPA capital verification report after the contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export-control screening flags on medical-device sales channels, particularly if a hospital buyer, distributor, or logistics provider is located in a comprehensively sanctioned country or a restricted end-user category.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Denied-party and restricted-party screening evidence for all transacting parties, product technical specification sheet demonstrating no dual-use role, end-user certificate from the final hospital or clinic, export control legal opinion from PRC counsel, healthcare compliance certification, and a written sanctions compliance manual with escalation protocols.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the Taiwan parent's equity contribution through SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's SAFE-registered FDI foreign-exchange capital account at the selected PRC Tier-1 bank. Before remitting, complete the SAFE foreign-investment information disclosure and FDI business registration, and obtain the FDI registration certificate or bank-entered registration number. The remittance instruction must carry a balance-of-payments purpose code for inbound foreign direct investment equity injection and include the WFOE's legal name, SAFE registration reference, and explicit reference to the capital contribution resolution. Upon receipt, the bank will perform capital verification, anti-money-laundering screening, and true-and-legal transaction certification before allowing settlement into RMB. Settlement must be supported by payroll, rental, equipment, raw-material, or licensing expenses. A licensed PRC CPA should issue a capital verification report after each paid-in tranche, and the WFOE should file the contribution and verification result with the market-regulation authority where required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For imports of medical-grade acrylic polymers, packaging, and high-precision lathe tooling, the WFOE may disburse through standard SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for low-value pre-payment or open-account settlement, commercial documentary collections for document-against-payment or document-against-acceptance flows, and irrevocable letters of credit opened by the domestic bank via SWIFT MT700 for large supplier contracts. Each outward remittance must be matched to an import customs declaration in the SAFE monitoring system, supported by commercial invoices, purchase contracts, bills of lading, and insurance certificates, and must bear the proper BOP current-account trade purpose code for goods imports. For RMB settlements with onshore Chinese suppliers, the WFOE may use the RMB clearing system; for USD, EUR, or TWD payments, the domestic bank will route through its correspondent banking network, CHIPS, Fedwire, or CIPS as appropriate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB foreign-exchange forward contracts with PRC Tier-1 banks, permitted only when supported by genuine current-account or capital-account exposure and approved underlying trade documents

Cross-currency swaps between RMB and USD or EUR for matching liquidity and debt-service profiles, limited to the maturity of the underlying business obligation and subject to SAFE real-demand validation
FX options purchased from a licensed onshore bank after suitability and real-demand genuineness testing, with no speculative naked options allowed

Non-deliverable forwards and offshore synthetic RMB products are not permissible as hedge instruments for the Chinese WFOE; any NDF hedge must be isolated in the foreign parent treasury and must not be booked through the PRC entity due to capital-control and SAFE restrictions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Information Declaration (Company Act Article 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (Company Registration and Information Platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15 January through 31 March each year for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Representative director is liable for a fine of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000 for failure to file or for incorrect filing; if the defect is not cured, the regulator may issue repeated fines. No direct strike-off but repeated non-compliance may be treated as a governance failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' General Meeting and Adoption of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' General Meeting (Company Registry / Ministry of Economic Affairs exercises supervisory enforcement only)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Representative director may be fined NT$10,000 to NT$50,000 by the competent authority; the authority may also order correction and re-fine for continued default. Failure to operate for six months after starting business can trigger a government order of dissolution under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May through 31 May of the year following the taxable year (special fiscal years within five months after the fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing after 31 May triggers a surcharge of 1% per two days up to 15% on the unpaid tax, plus interest on delayed payment. Under-reported or unreported tax may be penalized up to three times the undercharged tax. Persistent violation may lead to tax registration revocation; combined with six months' non-operation it is a statutory ground for administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding Tax Statements for Salaries, Rent, Interest, and Professional Fees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 31 January of the year following the payment year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Withholding agent failing to file or filing late is subject to a fine of up to one and one-half times the amount of tax withheld, plus mandatory late filing penalties; repeated violations can trigger intensified inspections and tax liens.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign (or Mainland China) Invested Enterprise Annual Operating Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year (by 31 March for calendar-year enterprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false reporting may result in an administrative order to cure, fines, and as a last resort suspension or revocation of the investment approval, which can lead to dissolution and forced deregistration of the Taiwan entity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent CPA audit of the annual financial statements is required under Taiwan Companies Act Article 20 and the MOEA announcement where the paid-in capital reaches or exceeds NT$30,000,000 (approximately USD 1,000,000). The only general quantitative trigger is capital; there is no general revenue or headcount threshold for private limited companies. Special mandatory audit rules apply to banks, insurance companies, securities firms, futures firms, and financial holding companies regardless of capital. The Taiwan Food and Drug Administration's QMS/GMP surveillance audit is a separate quality-system audit, not a financial-statement audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public companies must prepare financial statements in accordance with the Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS) endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission (Taiwan local GAAP for SMEs); publicly held companies must use Taiwan IFRS; an unlisted foreign-invested company may voluntarily elect IFRS from the approved set; income tax settlement is based on the Income Tax Act with book-tax adjustments.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan's beneficial-ownership/management information regime requires an annual electronic declaration between 15 January and 31 March to the Ministry of Economic Affairs, covering directors, supervisors, managers, and every shareholder holding 10% or more of share capital. Any change during the year, including a shareholding transfer that moves a shareholder across the 10% line, must be reported within 15 days of the change. There is no 30-day window under Taiwan law; the 15-day change reporting rule applies.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for accredited High and New Technology Enterprises (HNTE); 100% super deduction for qualifying R&D expenses (currently effective through 2025 and extended indefinitely by the State Council); reduced 20% preferential rate for Small Low-Profit Enterprises with taxable income up to RMB 3 million and headcount/assets thresholds; accelerated depreciation for fixed assets in medical device manufacturing; free-trade zone tax holidays may apply for specific pilot zones (e.g., Hainan, Shanghai Lingang) subject to operational substance requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A06301 (Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return – Form A, 2017 version) filed through the Electronic Tax Bureau (电子税务局) of the State Taxation Administration (STA); mandatory supplementary schedules (A100000, A105000, A107012, etc.) are uploaded electronically.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., by 31 May for calendar-year taxpayers). Provisional quarterly returns are due within 15 days after each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from principal operations – gross sales of intraocular acrylic lenses, consumables, and related services rendered during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All intercompany sales to the Taiwan parent or other affiliates must be recorded at arm's length prices as per the independent transaction principle. For a WFOE, revenue recognition should follow PRC GAAP; any transfer pricing adjustment upward or downward must be reconciled in the tax return. Cross-border invoices must align with customs declarations (if exported) and the foreign exchange settlement records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total cost of principal operations – direct materials (acrylic polymers, lathe consumables, packaging), direct labor, and manufacturing overhead allocated to lens production.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cost allocations from foreign affiliates (e.g., royalties for manufacturing process, technical service fees) must be supported by adequate contracts and actual service rendering. Unsupported charges to the Taiwan parent may be disallowed as deductions, and the tax authority may recharacterise them as constructive dividends, triggering WHT and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit – the pre-tax accounting profit determined under PRC GAAP on the income statement: operating profit plus non-operating income and minus non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE has a permanent establishment (PE) outside China or in Taiwan, the allocation of profits must be disclosed. For non-resident shareholders, this is the base figure before tax adjustments; confirm that no expenses attributable to tax-exempt income are deducted. The Taiwan parent's supervision board or auditor should verify the alignment of this number with audited financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment items – net amount of tax increases and decreases (e.g., non-deductible expenses, fair value changes, R&D super deduction, incentives, tax-exempt income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All adjustments must be documented in Schedule A105000. Cross-border interest and royalties paid to a Taiwan recipient must be limited to the arm's length amount; if the Taiwan lender/licensor is not beneficially entitled, the payment may be recharacterised as equity – disallowed as interest and treated as dividend subject to 10% WHT. Any underpayment arising from incorrect adjustments incurs daily late surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income – accounting profit after all adjustments and after deducting prior-year losses carried forward (limited to 5 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 5-year loss carryforward is a strict limitation; any carryforward from a year closed after filing must be evidenced by the prior year's return. For a WFOE with a Taiwan parent, ensure that the loss offset does not exceed the statutory period and that the loss was not generated by a transaction lacking economic substance. The tax authority may apply the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) to disallow loss compensation if the loss was artificially shifted via transfer pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable – taxable income multiplied by 25% (or reduced rate), less tax credits, foreign tax credits, and the sum of quarterly estimated payments; final amount due or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE qualifies for an HNTE certificate, the reduced 15% rate must be applied only after the certificate is filed with the STA. Foreign tax credits for Taiwan-source taxes (e.g., on dividends) are generally not acceptable under PRC law unless a treaty is in force; since the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement is not effective, no foreign tax credit for Taiwan taxes may be claimed. If the entity anticipates a refund, the non-resident shareholder must arrange for the repatriation of the refund after the final settlement, subject to 10% dividend WHT when the refund is distributed as profit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may be penalised under Art. 62 of the Taxation Administration Law (TAL) from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, and a separate penalty of RMB 200 per day (if late payment). Underpayment of tax attracts a daily late surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid amount, plus a monetary penalty ranging from 50% to 5 times the tax underpaid (Art. 63). Criminal liability for intentional underdeclaration of tax exceeding RMB 50,000 in a single year may constitute tax evasion under Art. 201 of the Criminal Law, with imprisonment up to 7 years and fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (PRC CIT Law Art. 37 and Implementation Regulation Art. 91) on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders. No treaty reduction is currently available for Taiwan residents because the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement has not been ratified by the PRC authorities and is not in force.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Since no effective tax treaty exists between the PRC and Taiwan, no claim for treaty-based WHT alleviation can be made. If dividends are routed through an intermediary jurisdiction (e.g., Hong Kong, Singapore) with a tax treaty, the non-resident shareholder must provide: (1) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the intermediate jurisdiction; (2) a Beneficial Ownership (BO) self-assessment statement (Form No. 501) demonstrating that the recipient has real economic substance (employees, functions, risks) and is not a conduit; (3) supporting documentation proving the 12-month holding period for reduced WHT (e.g., 5% under Hong Kong/China DTA if all conditions met); and (4) evidence that the payment is not linked to the Taiwan ultimate parent in a way that fails the limitation-on-benefits clause. The PRC payer must file the withholding return and remit the reduced WHT only after the tax authority accepts the BO filing.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on cross-border interest and royalties is 10% for each category. Under applicable treaties (e.g., with Hong Kong), the rate may be reduced to 7% for royalties and 7% for interest (subject to the DTA's limitations); however, for Taiwan recipients the statutory 10% continues to apply. Any rate reduction requires a valid TRC, BO documentation, and a submission of the withholding return (Form F) through the electronic tax portal.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (contemporaneous documentation) is mandatory if any of the following thresholds are met in a fiscal year: RMB 200 million for related-party tangible asset transfers; RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers; RMB 100 million for intangible asset transfers; or RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions (including service fees, interest, and royalties). A Master File is required when aggregate related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Under PRC CIT Law Art. 47, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and the doctrine of substance-over-form apply. The tax authority may reclassify or disregard an arrangement lacking economic substance. For a WFOE engaged in high-precision manufacturing, Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) — including production planning, quality assurance, key equipment operation, and supply-chain decisions — must be performed within China to justify the profit attributable to the WFOE. If the Taiwan parent retains decision-making power over critical functions and risks without compensating the WFOE adequately, the tax authority may allocate a higher share of profits to the WFOE under the profit split method. Additionally, under the 2017 Transfer Pricing Circular (Bulletin No. 6 of 2017), the WFOE must prepare annual TP documentation and include a TP analysis on related-party transactions in the annual filing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE fails to prepare, maintain, or present its Local File or Master File within 20 days after the tax authority's written request, despite exceeding the statutory thresholds. Further, it submits documentation that omits or misrepresents the actual contractual terms, comparability data, or intercompany price adjustments, with the intent of understating China-source taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Levying and Collection of Tax Law (TAL) Art. 44, the tax authority may apply a deemed profit method and adjust the entity's taxable income; additionally, a penalty of RMB 10,000 or more may be imposed under TAL Art. 62 for failure to keep conforming books. If the documented data is false, the adjustment is treated as evasion under TAL Art. 63 – the taxpayer is liable for 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax, plus daily overdue surcharge at 0.05%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed or instructed the preparation of false transfer pricing files are personally liable for the resultant underpaid tax and penalties. Civil asset recovery may be enforced against a director's personal assets if the company is used as a mere instrument ('piercing the corporate veil' under PRC Company Law Art. 20 / 2023 Art. 23). The director may be banned from leaving China (travel ban) under the exit control mechanism, and criminal liability for tax evasion under Criminal Law Art. 201 – up to 7 years' imprisonment – may attach.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE issues or obtains fraudulent special value-added tax (VAT) invoices for non-existent R&D services, packaging materials, or equipment purchases, often to shift profits to a shell supplier controlled by the Taiwan parent, or to inflate deductible expenses and claim false export VAT rebates for acrylic lens exports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Law Art. 205 imposes a fine ranging from RMB 50,000 up to 5 times the tax amount involved on the entity; for persons directly in charge, life imprisonment can be imposed for particularly large amounts. Tax authorities may also invoke TAL Art. 63, imposing 50%–5 times the underpaid tax and full denial of the claimed deductions. If the scheme involves export refund fraud, additional penalties under the Export Tax Refund Administration rules apply (Art. 22 of the State Council Order No. 401).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, CFOs, or tax agents who orchestrated the false invoice scheme are directly exposed to criminal liability for tax evasion and invoice fraud. Corporate veil piercing is readily applied if bank accounts or assets were commingled with personal accounts. A director's personal property may be seized for unpaid taxes and criminal fines. A travel ban and suspension from serving as a corporate officer are mandatory court measures; imprisonment of up to life can be imposed for leaders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays dividends to the Taiwan parent without withholding the 10% corporate income tax, or disguises the distribution as intercompany loan repayment, consulting fees, or royalties to avoid the withholding obligation. In another variant, dividends are routed through a Hong Kong agent with no employees, premises, or business activities, solely to obtain the 5% DTA rate on dividends to the Hong Kong agent while the ultimate beneficiary remains in Taiwan.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under CIT Law Art. 37, the WFOE is jointly and severally liable for the withholding obligation. Failure to withhold triggers a penalty of 50% to 3 times the tax that was not withheld under TAL Art. 69, plus the unpaid WHT itself and daily surcharge. If the conduit arrangement is detected, the GAAR (CIT Law Art. 47) will recharacterise the Hong Kong entity as a shell – denying treaty benefits and treating the entire amount as a Chinese-source dividend subject to 10% WHT, plus an additional 50% penalty for fraud/evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: For design or facilitation of the non-withholding scheme, directors are personally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties. Courts may pierce the veil if the company acts as an alter ego of the Taiwan shareholder, allowing creditors or the tax authority to satisfy the department's claims out of directors' personal assets. Directors who signed the dividend resolution or foreign exchange transfers may additionally face criminal prosecution for tax evasion (Art. 201) and for illegal foreign exchange dealings (Art. 175 / 225), carrying imprisonment of 3 to 10 years and substantial fines. They are also subject to a court-ordered travel ban and blacklisting in personal credit records.
